# Code of Conduct

## The short version

Be decent to people. This is a small project maintained by one person in their
spare time; treat the issue tracker as somebody else's workshop that you have
been invited into.

## What is expected

- **Assume good faith.** A bug report that turns out to be user error, and a
  reply that turns out to be wrong, are both normal. Neither deserves scorn.
- **Be specific rather than annoyed.** "It doesn't work" costs everyone time.
  The version, the OS, the link you pasted, and the exact error text usually
  solve the problem in one round.
- **Accept "no" as an answer.** Not every request fits the project. A declined
  feature is a scoping decision, not a personal slight.
- **Remember nobody is on the clock.** There is no support contract here. An
  unanswered issue means someone is busy, not that they are ignoring you.

## What is not acceptable

- Harassment, insults, or personal attacks — including about someone's
  nationality, gender, sexuality, religion, disability, or appearance.
- Sexual language or imagery.
- Publishing someone's private information.
- Sustained disruption: reopening settled arguments, brigading, or spamming.
- Pressuring anyone into helping you bypass a site's terms of service or into
  supporting infringement. See the disclaimer in the [README](README.md) — this
  project is for content you have the right to save, and requests that assume
  otherwise are off-topic.

## Scope

This applies in the issue tracker, pull requests, commit comments, and any
other space where someone is participating in this project.

## Enforcement

Report a problem by opening an issue, or privately via
[GitHub's report abuse form](https://github.com/contact/report-abuse) if the
issue tracker is not appropriate.

Reports are handled by the maintainer. Responses range from a request to stop,
to editing or deleting the offending content, to blocking the account from the
repository — chosen to fit what actually happened. Because there is exactly one
maintainer, there is no appeals board; what there is instead is a commitment to
read the whole thread before acting rather than reacting to the last message.

## Attribution

Adapted in spirit from the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org),
rewritten for a single-maintainer project rather than adopted verbatim.
